title.en: Moment of inertia and kinematics of rotational motion
title.kn: ಜಡತ್ವ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ ಮತ್ತು ಭ್ರಮಣ ಚಲನೆಯ ಚಲನಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ

hook.en: The heavy flywheel of an engine is hard to start and hard to stop. In rotation, it is not just the mass but how far that mass is from the axis that matters.
hook.kn: ಎಂಜಿನ್‌ನ ಭಾರವಾದ ಫ್ಲೈವೀಲ್ ಅನ್ನು ತಿರುಗಿಸಲೂ ಕಷ್ಟ, ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಲೂ ಕಷ್ಟ. ಭ್ರಮಣದಲ್ಲಿ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಮಾತ್ರವಲ್ಲ, ಅದು ಅಕ್ಷದಿಂದ ಎಷ್ಟು ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿದೆ ಎಂಬುದೂ ಮುಖ್ಯ.

body.en: The kinetic energy of a rotating body is $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$, where $I = \sum m_i r_i^2$ is its *moment of inertia* about the axis. It plays the role of mass in rotation and depends on the mass, how the mass is distributed and the axis chosen. The radius of gyration k is defined by $I = Mk^2$.
body.kn: ತಿರುಗುವ ಕಾಯದ ಚಲನ ಶಕ್ತಿ K = ½Iω², ಇಲ್ಲಿ I = Σmᵢrᵢ² ಜಡತ್ವ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ. ಭ್ರಮಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದು ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಯ ಪಾತ್ರ ವಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ, ಅದರ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅಕ್ಷವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಭ್ರಮಣ ತ್ರಿಜ್ಯ k: I = Mk².

title.en: Moment of inertia and rotational kinematics

say.en: Moment of inertia adds up each mass times the square of its distance from the axis. It plays the role of mass in rotation.
For the same mass and radius, a ring has more moment of inertia than a disc, because all its mass is far from the axis.

text.en: Same mass: ring is hardest to spin

say.en: With constant angular acceleration, the equations are the linear ones with x, v and a replaced by theta, omega and alpha.
Example: a wheel starts from rest with alpha equal to 2 radians per second squared. After 10 seconds, omega is 20 and it has turned 100 radians, about 16 turns.

narration.en: A body rolling without slipping shares its energy between moving and turning. With moment of inertia I = kMR², its acceleration is g sin θ/(1 + k), whatever its mass or radius. A ring (k = 1) is slowest; a solid sphere (k = 2/5) wins.
narration.kn: ಜಾರದೆ ಉರುಳುವ ಕಾಯ ತನ್ನ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಾನಾಂತರ ಮತ್ತು ಭ್ರಮಣದ ನಡುವೆ ಹಂಚುತ್ತದೆ. ಜಡತ್ವದ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ I = kMR² ಆದರೆ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ g sin θ/(1 + k), ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅಥವಾ ತ್ರಿಜ್ಯ ಏನೇ ಇರಲಿ. ಉಂಗುರ (k = 1) ಅತಿ ನಿಧಾನ; ಘನ ಗೋಳ (k = 2/5) ಗೆಲ್ಲುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Kinematics of rotation about a fixed axis

body.en: With constant angular acceleration α, the equations mirror those of linear *motion*: $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$, $\theta = \omega_0 t + \tfrac12\alpha t^2$ and $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\theta$. Just replace x by θ, v by ω and a by α.
body.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ ಕೋನೀಯ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ α ಇದ್ದಾಗ ಸಮೀಕರಣಗಳು ರೇಖೀಯ ಚಲನೆಯಂತೆಯೇ: ω = ω₀ + αt, θ = ω₀t + ½αt², ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ.

narration.en: With constant angular acceleration α, the equations mirror those of linear motion: $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$, $\theta = \omega_0 t + \tfrac12\alpha t^2$ and $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\theta$. Just replace x by θ, v by ω and a by α.
narration.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ ಕೋನೀಯ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ α ಇದ್ದಾಗ ಸಮೀಕರಣಗಳು ರೇಖೀಯ ಚಲನೆಯಂತೆಯೇ: ω = ω₀ + αt, θ = ω₀t + ½αt², ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ.

say.en: With constant angular acceleration alpha, the equations mirror those of linear motion: omega equals omega 0 plus alpha t, theta equals omega 0 t plus tfrac 12 alpha t squared and omega squared equals omega 0 squared plus 2 alpha theta. Just replace x by theta, v by omega and a by alpha. Revolutions equals theta / 2 pi.
say.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ ಕೋನೀಯ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ alpha ಇದ್ದಾಗ ಸಮೀಕರಣಗಳು ರೇಖೀಯ ಚಲನೆಯಂತೆಯೇ: omega equals omega 0 plus alpha t, theta equals omega 0t plus one half alpha t squared, omega squared equals omega 0 squared plus 2 alpha theta.

problem.en: The angular speed of a motor wheel rises from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 s. Find its angular acceleration and the number of revolutions it makes in this time.

steps.en: θ = ω₀t + ½αt² = 640π + 512π = 1152π rad, i.e. 1152π/2π = 576 revolutions.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The angular speed of a motor wheel rises from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 s. Find its angular acceleration and the number of revolutions it makes in this time.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The angular speed of a motor wheel rises from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. Find its angular acceleration and the number of revolutions it makes in this time.
omega 0 equals 2 pi times 1200 over 60 equals 40 pi rad/s; omega equals 2 pi times 3120 over 60 equals 104 pi rad/s.
alpha equals 104 pi minus 40 pi/16 equals 4 pi is approximately 12.6 rad/s squared.
theta equals omega 0t plus one half alpha t squared equals 640 pi plus 512 pi equals 1152 pi rad, i.e. 1152 pi /2 pi equals 576 revolutions.
So the answer is alpha equals 4 pi rad/s squared; 576 revolutions.

problem.en: Two 1 kg masses are fixed at the ends of a light 2 m rod. Find the moment of inertia about an axis through the centre perpendicular to the rod.

steps.en: Each mass is 1 m from the axis.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Two 1 kg masses are fixed at the ends of a light 2 m rod. Find the moment of inertia about an axis through the centre perpendicular to the rod.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Two 1 kilogram masses are fixed at the ends of a light 2 metres rod. Find the moment of inertia about an axis through the centre perpendicular to the rod.
Each mass is 1 metre from the axis.
I equals 1 times 1 squared plus 1 times 1 squared equals 2 kilograms m squared.
So the answer is 2 kilograms m squared.

body.en: x → θ, v → ω, a → α, m → I, F → τ, p → L. Every linear formula has a rotational twin: ½mv² → ½Iω², F = ma → τ = Iα, p = mv → L = Iω.

narration.en: Linear ↔ rotational dictionary. x → θ, v → ω, a → α, m → I, F → τ, p → L. Every linear formula has a rotational twin: ½mv² → ½Iω², F = ma → τ = Iα, p = mv → L = Iω.

mnemonic.en: Swap the letters, keep the formula.

say.en: Linear ↔ rotational dictionary. x gives theta, v gives omega, a gives alpha, m gives I, F gives tau, p gives L. Every linear formula has a rotational twin: one half mv squared gives one half I omega squared, F equals ma gives tau equals I alpha, p equals mv gives L equals I omega.
